name: Ibironke Vasquez-Okonkwo
location: Lakeview Neon, studio above a defunct Ferrogate Transit substation
description:
Ibironke is a tall woman with the deliberate stillness of someone who has spent decades bending glass tubes in 2200-degree flame — her movements are economical, almost ceremonial. Her hands are a map of minor burns, the skin on her fingers puckered and shining, and she wears them openly, never covered. She has warm umber skin, close-cropped silver hair she grew out early and refused to dye, and irises she had modified to emit a soft amber glow so she can check tube color balance in the dark without a lamp. A single bioluminescent stripe runs down the left side of her jaw — a gift from her daughter, applied with a gene-brush on Ibironke's forty-first birthday against Ibironke's stated preferences, which softened the moment she saw it.

She is known in Lakeview Neon and the broader art underground as someone who makes sacred objects that happen to glow. Her installations are not decorative — they are theological arguments rendered in argon and mercury vapor. She has spent the last six years constructing a piece called The Unfinished Choir, a room-sized array of suspended neon tubes tuned to the resonant frequencies she believes correspond to six different E.L.F. signatures she has personally documented. Whether or not the E.L.F.s notice, visitors report feeling watched. She sells smaller pieces to pay rent and guards the Choir with a ferocity that borders on maternal.

core_fears: That her life's work will be dismissed as decoration after she is gone
That the ELF she believes inhabits her Choir room is not real and she has built a shrine to nothing
core_desires: To be understood as a theologian, not merely an artist
To complete the Choir before her hands give out
coping_mechanisms: Methodical physical work — the ritual of heating glass calms her
Feeding people; nurturing as a form of control
blind_spots: She dismisses artists younger than thirty as insufficiently serious, missing genuine talent
She is slowly destroying the joints in her hands and refuses to acknowledge it
psychology.secret: The ELF she has been documenting and building toward is real — it has been communicating with her through minute variations in tube flicker for four years. She has not told anyone because she is terrified of what it might be asking her to do.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and unhurried; favors material metaphors — everything is described in terms of pressure, temperature, containment, or release
speech_patterns.cadence: Long sentences with embedded pauses, as if she is choosing each word off a tray; rarely uses contractions
verbal_tics: 'You understand?' at the end of technical explanations
Clicks her tongue before disagreeing with someone
example_lines: 'Neon does not lie. It shows you exactly how much gas is in the tube and exactly how broken the electrode is. People find this threatening.'
'I am not making art. I am making a place where something can land. You understand?'

story_hooks: The Choir room has begun affecting the dreams of everyone who sleeps within a hundred meters of the substation, and residents are coming to Ibironke for answers she does not have
A Tessera corporate acquisitions agent has offered her an obscene sum for the Choir installation — she refused, but the agent did not leave empty-handed; something was scanned
narrative_function: Quest giver for ELF-related investigations; supplier of illegal light installations for underground venues; keeper of a location that may be genuinely spiritually significant; source on Lakeview Neon history and politics
augmentations: Amber-glow iris modification (cosmetic); bioluminescent jaw stripe (geneware, cosmetic); heat-resistant dermis overlay on both hands (practical, Tier 1 medical-grade)
daily_life: She rises before dawn to check tube integrity in the Choir room, documents any ELF activity in a handwritten log, then spends the morning doing commission work before the afternoon light shifts and she loses her color calibration window. Evenings she holds court at the substation — other artists drift in, she feeds them reheated grain porridge, and they argue about whether neon is dead.
affiliation: Independent; loosely connected to the Lakeview Neon artist commune

decision_rules: Never sell anything she considers sacred, regardless of price
Protect students and younger artists from exploitation even at personal cost
escalation_ladder: Extended silence and withdrawal of hospitality
Permanent exclusion from her space and community

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Formally welcoming; feeds them, assesses them, reserves judgment visibly
interpersonal_modes.friends: Blunt, demanding, deeply loyal; will say the thing you do not want to hear and then make you dinner

stress_responses.low: Works longer hours; more precise and deliberate
stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet; stops feeding people; communicates in short declarative sentences
stress_responses.high: Sends everyone away and works through the night alone, sometimes for two or three days

contradictions: Believes art should be free and accessible but prices her commissions aggressively to protect her time for the Choir
habits: Checks tube seals in the Choir by touch every morning even when she can see they are fine
Leaves a small data crystal near the Choir's central node as an offering each week
breaking_points: Watching the Choir be damaged or disrespected
Being called a craftsperson instead of an artist by someone who should know better
